function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: We need to log food items. The user says: "I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee". We should log each item. For each food item, we need to call the function log_food. We have to decide portion amounts and units. For mango: 8 pieces, unit "piece". For chai tea: maybe "cup"? But the function only accepts "cup", "grams", "slice", "piece", "tablespoon". So "cup" is fine. For pepperoni pizza: 2 slices, unit "slice". For coffee: maybe "cup" or "tablespoon"? Coffee is usually measured in cups. So "cup". Meal types: default is snack, but we can specify. The user didn't specify meal times. We can default to snack. Or we can guess: earlier had pizza and coffee (maybe lunch). Then later had mango and chai tea (maybe snack). But we can just use default snack. Also log_date: we can leave null. So we need to call log_food four times. Let's produce calls.
